To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the redox potential of the mediator is the main determinant for the performance of the glucose enzyme electrode and that the redox mediator can be tuned for this application by changing the ligand.
we report on a simple and versatile approach for the fabrication of enzyme electrodes, demonstrated for glucose oxidase, using a cross-linking methodology to prepare films on graphite.

cross-linked enzyme electrodes have been fabricated by immobilizing glucose oxidase in films of polyallylamine, a di-epoxy cross-linker, and redox mediators of the Os(bipy)2(4-amino methyl pyridine) complex type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials and methods for the construction of biosensors and bioelectrodes, with a particular focus on glucose biosensors and enzymatic fuel cells.
the development of novel, versatile methodology for the preparation of enzyme electrodes and their application to the development of glucose biosensors and enzymatic fuel cells.
the development of novel, versatile and robust methods for the immobilisation of enzymes on electrodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the approach described in this work provides an effective method to optimise enzyme electrodes by evaluation of glucose responses as a function of the ratio of the redox mediator, the polyallylamine cross-linker and the glucose oxidase enzyme, in films cross-linked using a novel di-epoxide cross-linker.
the approach of cross-linking enzyme and redox mediator is a viable route to the preparation of mediated glucose enzyme electrodes.
the work described here has demonstrated a novel and versatile approach for the fabrication of glucose biosensors based on cross-linked films of osmium complexes and glucose oxidases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new method of immobilizing enzymes on electrodes has been developed.

the use of a cross-linked enzyme electrode (CLEE) approach to prepare glucose electrodes using functionalised osmium redox complex mediators has been demonstrated, with a range of complexes synthesised, evaluated and compared in the context of glucose biosensors.
the cross-linked films of osmium complexes and enzyme on electrodes can be used to prepare glucose electrodes with a wide range of electrochemical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated that cross-linked films of osmium complexes and glucose oxidases can be prepared on graphite electrodes, and that the redox potential of the complexes can be varied by substitution of ligands to achieve lower oxidation potentials for glucose oxidation, with a consequent lowering of the applied potential required for glucose biosensors.
the cross-linked films are stable and can be used for long term glucose sensing.

the cross-linking methodology is a versatile approach to prepare mediated enzyme electrodes and that it is possible to tune the electrocatalytic properties by varying the ratio of the enzyme to the redox mediator and the cross-linking reagents, and the redox potential of the mediator by using ligands of varying electron donating ability.
